signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the units of the reported number and compare them with the units of a rate.
signals.name: Increment quotient written with the denominator omitted
signals.observation: The change in the function over the increment is computed and the division by the increment is not carried out.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to evaluate the shifted term at one numerical increment and compare it with the written expression.
signals.name: Increment added to the function value rather than to the input
signals.observation: The increment is attached outside the function instead of inside its argument.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what quantity was divided by what to produce the reported number.
signals.name: Difference of outputs reported as the rate
signals.observation: The two function values are subtracted and the result is given without the division by the change in input.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which input is the starting one and check that both differences begin there.
signals.name: Endpoints subtracted in opposite orders above and below the line
signals.observation: The numerator is formed in one order and the denominator in the other, so the sign of the rate is reversed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what division was performed and what unit that division produces.
signals.name: Units copied from the table header
signals.observation: The rate is reported with the units of the modelled quantity rather than of its rate of change.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to finish the sentence naming what changes and per what.
signals.name: Value computed correctly with no statement of meaning
signals.observation: The number is right and the response does not say what it means for the situation.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask over which interval the described number was computed.
signals.name: Average rate described as the rate at a moment
signals.observation: The response says an interval average is what the quantity is doing at a single instant.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two requires two inputs and which requires one.
signals.name: Two terms distinguished by name only
signals.observation: The response repeats the two names without saying which one involves an interval.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether any particular increment appears in the written expression.
signals.name: Small increment used in place of a limit
signals.observation: The instantaneous rate is written as the quotient at a very small increment rather than as a limit.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which quantity is being made small in the expression.
signals.name: Limit written over the wrong variable
signals.observation: The limit symbol is attached to the base point rather than to the increment.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether each written line is a true statement on its own.
signals.name: Limit symbol attached only to the final line
signals.observation: The quotient is manipulated without the limit symbol and the symbol is written once at the end.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the requested object accepts inputs or is a single number.
signals.name: Derivative at a point written as a function of the variable
signals.observation: The expression carries the running variable where the base point belongs, so a function is produced where a number was asked for.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which input makes the numerator vanish.
signals.name: Second input made to approach the wrong value
signals.observation: The limit is written as the second input approaches zero rather than the base point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the denominator must equal so that the quotient measures a slope between the two named points.
signals.name: Two point form written with the increment denominator
signals.observation: The numerator uses the two point form and the denominator keeps the increment.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the top of the Leibniz form would mean on its own.
signals.name: Leibniz form separated into two quantities
signals.observation: The response splits the notation and cancels parts of it as though it were a fraction.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which written symbol names a number and which names a rule.
signals.name: Derivative function and its value written with the same symbol
signals.observation: The prime form with an argument and the prime form alone are used interchangeably in one response.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to say what the read slope means for the quantity the graph records.
signals.name: Graphical reading given with no numerical or verbal counterpart
signals.observation: The slope is read from the graph correctly and the requested interpretation in words is not produced.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the sentence describes a height or a steepness.
signals.name: Verbal description given for the quantity rather than its rate
signals.observation: The sentence describes how large the quantity is instead of how fast it is changing.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which of the two computed numbers measures steepness.
signals.name: Function value used as the slope
signals.observation: The height of the curve at the point is reported as the slope of the tangent line.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what else besides the slope is needed to write the line.
signals.name: Slope stated correctly with the tangent line never written
signals.observation: The derivative value is identified as the slope and the requested line equation is not formed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to point to the two rows the question names before computing.
signals.name: Adjacent rows used in place of the named interval
signals.observation: The estimate is formed from the closest pair of rows rather than the pair the question names.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which rows bracket the point in question.
signals.name: Rows chosen on one side of the point only
signals.observation: A pair of rows both lying above the point is used to estimate the rate at the point.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the reported number came from the height of the curve or from its steepness.
signals.name: Function height read where the slope was requested
signals.observation: The value of the curve at the point is reported as the estimated derivative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which two points on the graph were used and how close they are to the point in question.
signals.name: Slope read from a secant far from the point
signals.observation: The estimate is formed from two widely separated points on the curve rather than from the local steepness.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the supplied function is continuous at the point in question.
signals.name: Example given that is not continuous at the point
signals.observation: The response supplies a function with a break rather than a continuous function with a corner.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for the slope just left and just right of the point in the supplied example.
signals.name: Example named with no reason for the failure
signals.observation: A suitable function is named and the response does not say why the derivative fails there.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the slope of a vertical line is.
signals.name: Vertical tangent read as a very large derivative
signals.observation: The response reports a large numerical slope at a point where the tangent line is vertical.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what each one sided slope does as the point is approached.
signals.name: Vertical tangent conflated with a corner
signals.observation: The failure is attributed to differing one sided slopes where the two sides both grow without bound.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the break implies for the existence of the derivative there.
signals.name: Discontinuity noted with no conclusion about the derivative
signals.observation: The break is identified correctly and the response does not draw the consequence for differentiability.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask for a continuous function whose derivative fails at a point.
signals.name: Implication used in the wrong direction
signals.observation: The response concludes that the function is differentiable because it is continuous.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the denominator equals after that substitution.
signals.name: Increment set to zero before the common factor is divided out
signals.observation: The substitution is made while the increment still stands in the denominator.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask where the increment appears in the written work.
signals.name: Rule applied and presented as a derivation from the definition
signals.observation: The power rule result is written under a heading naming the limit definition, with no quotient formed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the graph of the constant term alone looks like and what its slope is.
signals.name: Constant term carried unchanged into the derivative
signals.observation: The constant appears in the answer exactly as it appeared in the original expression.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the term changes when the variable changes.
signals.name: Constant treated as a power of the variable
signals.observation: The power rule is applied to the constant as though the variable were present with exponent zero in the wrong position.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to check the coefficient by differentiating the expanded form.
signals.name: Constant multiplied into the derivative twice
signals.observation: The constant is pulled out and also left inside the differentiated expression.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the term still depends on the variable once the coefficient is removed.
signals.name: Constant factor differentiated to zero along with the term
signals.observation: The response applies the constant rule to the coefficient and reports zero for the whole term.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to mark the sign in front of each term before differentiating.
signals.name: Terms differentiated and a sign lost in the difference
signals.observation: Each term is differentiated correctly and the subtraction between them is written as an addition.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which terms are joined by addition and which by multiplication.
signals.name: Sum rule pattern carried over to a product
signals.observation: A product in the expression is differentiated factor by factor in the way the sum was handled.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to differentiate one squared term from the limit definition and compare.
signals.name: Exponent lowered with the multiplying factor omitted
signals.observation: Each power has its exponent reduced by one and none carries the original exponent as a factor.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the derivative of the constant term alone is.
signals.name: Constant term left in place while the powers are differentiated
signals.observation: The variable terms are handled correctly and the constant survives into the derivative.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which part of the expression carries the variable, the base or the exponent.
signals.name: Natural exponential differentiated by the power rule
signals.observation: The exponent is reduced by one and a factor of the exponent is written in front.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the exponent is and what its derivative is.
signals.name: Exponential kept unchanged where a chain factor is required
signals.observation: The exponential is copied unchanged although its exponent is not the plain variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what kind of function the expression is before any rule is chosen.
signals.name: Logarithm differentiated as a power
signals.observation: The response treats the logarithm as a power of the variable and reduces an exponent.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what the argument of the logarithm is and whether it is the plain variable.
signals.name: Reciprocal written without the inner derivative
signals.observation: The reciprocal of the argument is written and the derivative of that argument is omitted.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to expand a short product, differentiate the expansion, and compare.
signals.name: Derivatives of the two factors multiplied together
signals.observation: The response reports the product of the two derivatives as the derivative of the product.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask how many terms the rule produces and how many appear in the answer.
signals.name: One of the two product rule terms omitted
signals.observation: The rule is set up correctly and only one of the two terms reaches the answer line.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the expression as written is a product or a sum of terms.
signals.name: Product rule applied to a product that is already expanded
signals.observation: The expanded polynomial is regrouped into a product and the rule is applied to it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the two factors can be multiplied out at all.
signals.name: Expansion chosen where a factor is not polynomial
signals.observation: The response attempts to multiply out a product containing a transcendental factor and then differentiates term by term.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to apply the rule to a quotient whose derivative is known and check the sign.
signals.name: Numerator terms written in the reverse order
signals.observation: The subtraction in the numerator is carried out with the two products exchanged.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask what power the denominator carries in the rule as stated.
signals.name: Denominator written without its square
signals.observation: The rule is set up correctly and the denominator appears to the first power.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to label each substituted number with the symbol it stands for.
signals.name: Function value substituted where a derivative value belongs
signals.observation: One of the four supplied numbers is placed in a position calling for the other kind of value.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask at which input the derivative is being evaluated and check every substituted value against it.
signals.name: Values substituted at different inputs
signals.observation: The four numbers are taken from more than one row of the table or more than one point on the graph.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask whether the denominator changes when the variable changes.
signals.name: Full quotient rule applied to a constant denominator
signals.observation: The fraction bar triggers the rule although the denominator carries no variable.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to check the rewriting at one convenient input.
signals.name: Constant pulled out with its reciprocal placed incorrectly
signals.observation: The rewriting multiplies by the constant instead of dividing by it.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which rule applies once the expression is written as one function over another.
signals.name: Rewritten quotient differentiated term by term
signals.observation: The sine and cosine forms are produced correctly and the numerator and denominator are then differentiated separately.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to check the rewriting at one convenient angle.
signals.name: Reciprocal and cofunction identities exchanged
signals.observation: The rewriting names the wrong quotient, for instance placing cosine over sine where the reverse was needed.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to derive the result from the reciprocal form and see where the sign arises.
signals.name: Negative sign omitted from the cosecant derivative
signals.observation: The product form is produced correctly for both functions and the sign is attached to neither.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to name the two standard functions the answer should be written with.
signals.name: Result left in quotient form with no product written
signals.observation: The quotient rule output is correct and is never rewritten in the standard product form when that is requested.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask which rule the rewritten expression is meant to be handed to.
signals.name: Identity chosen that leaves an expression no available rule handles
signals.observation: A correct identity is applied and the rewritten form still contains a quotient the response does not differentiate.

signals.distinguish_by: Ask the student to test the identity at one convenient angle before differentiating.
signals.name: Expression rewritten incorrectly so the derivative belongs to another function
signals.observation: The identity used is not valid and the derivative that follows is correct for the rewritten form only.
